title: US Supreme Court rules school segregation unconstitutional
summary: In Brown v. Board of Education, the Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools violated the Constitution.
reason: The NAACP, led in court by Thurgood Marshall, had challenged the separate but equal doctrine for years.
significance: The ruling was a turning point of the civil rights movement.
participants: Supreme Court of the United States
place: Supreme Court Building, Washington, D.C., United States
